newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil eases but finds support.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil eases but finds support.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps eased slightly late afternoon on Friday from firmer morning quotes in lacklustre trading, brokers said.
"It is extremely quiet with only a few traders around while the Japanese are still on holiday," reasoned one broker.
"Levels have eased a little bit but it looks like there is support," said another broker.
The front month January eased by 10 cents to $32.00/$32.25 per barrel from the morning's quotes.

The Singapore market had opened firmer after its two day break, up from Tuesday's $31.90/$32.00, as it took its cue from the higher overnight gas oil on the International Petroleum Exchange which closed a hefty $8.25 per tonne higher at $232.00 per tonne.
February gas oil was traded at midday at $31.15 and $31.16 per barrel while a February/March time spread was recorded at 90 cents, brokers said.
Fuel oil and naphtha were largely unchanged from Tuesday in quiet trading with January fuel oil quoted notionally at $120.50/$122.00 per tonne and naphtha at $24.80/$25.00 per barrel.
